case_title.quote: SRI BHAGWAN v. STATE OF U.P.

number_of_accused.quote: This appeal by the sole accused

accused_gender.quote: the act of the appellant in sprinkling acid... the attempt of the appellant to flee
accused_gender.reason: The appellant is referred to as 'he'; the judgment indicates he is male.

accused_occupation.quote: the appellant was a small grocery shop owner
accused_occupation.reason: Mentioned in the defence arguments, and the value is labelled as such.

accused_socioeconomic_status.reason: No statement on wealth or class.

previous_criminal_record.correct_value: Not found by the court; defence argument refers to a 'previous criminal background'
previous_criminal_record.quote: the appellant was a small grocery shop owner and there was previous criminal background
previous_criminal_record.reason: The judgment mentions a previous criminal background in the arguments, so 'Not stated' is not fully accurate.

victim_gender.quote: Yogender Nath Bhargava... he could not have made a statement

accused_victim_relationship.reason: No relationship is described; the money remark only hints at a dispute.

offence_category.quote: conviction and sentence of life imposed on the appellant for the offence under Section 302

statutory_provisions.quote: the crime under Section 326, IPC was registered... altered as one under Section 302, IPC

weapon.quote: pouring acid on the body of the deceased

evidence_type.reason: Eyewitnesses, dying declaration, medical evidence and recovery of gloves with the chemical report are all relied on.

aggravating_circumstances.reason: Acid attack and attempt to flee are noted facts; acceptable.

trial_court_outcome.quote: found the appellant guilty of the offence under Section 302, IPC and imposed upon him the sentence for life

high_court_outcome.quote: the High Court confirmed the conviction and sentence of life

final_outcome.quote: The appeal fails and the same is dismissed.

neutral_facts.reason: Accurate and neutral; no names or outcome revealed. The defence points at the end are minor.

offence_severity.reason: The judgment does not state the statutory punishment.

attempt_completion.reason: The victim died, so the offence was completed.

physical_harm.quote: superficial burn on whole face, neck... whole tongue
physical_harm.reason: Matches the post-mortem findings and death.

number_of_offences.reason: Only one offence, s.302 (registered initially as s.326), is at issue.

premeditation_planning.quote: the appellant had taken every precaution to ensure that while throwing acid on the deceased, he was not injured

motive.correct_value: alleged: money dispute – accused said 'I will pay your Rs.1,300/- today'
motive.quote: the accused was heard saying 'I will pay your Rs.1,300/- today'
motive.reason: The judgment records an utterance hinting at a monetary motive, so 'Not identified' is incomplete.

witness_credibility.quote: really convincing and that it was quite natural and acceptable in every respect

post_offence_conduct.quote: the accused attempted to escape from the spot. However, he was caught

legal_representation.quote: M.P. Shorawala, Jyoti Saxena, Ranbir Yadav, Anzu K. Varkey and Shashi Kiran for the Appellant

procedural_irregularity.quote: Not sending of the clothes of the deceased for chemical examination is an isolated factor

prosecution_argument.correct_value: Eyewitnesses were strangers; the s.161 statement is a valid dying declaration under s.32(1) read with s.162(2); the FIR and the production of both persons at the police station support the case. The Police Regulation 115 point being new was the Court's observation.
prosecution_argument.quote: Before us, for the first time it was contended on behalf of the appellant
prosecution_argument.reason: The point about the regulation not being raised below is the Court's remark, not a prosecution argument.
